title: RAMESH CHANDRA YADAV versus DOIWALA SUGAR COMPANY LIMITED
judges: ["Hon'ble Shri Justice Manoj Kumar Gupta,Hon'ble Mr. Justice Subhash Upadhyay"]

IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
THE HON'BLE CHIEF JUSTICE MR. MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA
AND
THE HON'BLE JUSTICE MR. SUBHASH UPADHYAY
Special Appeal No.276 of 2026
Ramesh Chandra Yadav ----Appellant
Versus
Doiwala Sugar Company Limited & Another ----Respondents
September 18, 2026
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. Dharmendra Barthwal, learned counsel for the appellant
None present for the respondents
JUDGMENT : (per Mr. Manoj Kumar Gupta, C. J.)
1. The present intra-court appeal is directed against the
order passed by learned Single Judge dated 07.09.2021 in WPMS
No.2878/2015. The office has reported a delay of 1713 days in
preferring the instant appeal. The sole explanation given in the
affidavit filed in support of the application is that the appeal has
been filed after hectic effort by the appellant to obtain relevant
papers and after the papers became available, he approached his
counsel in the month of "March and April, 2026".
2. The writ petition before the learned Single Judge was
by non-appellant no.1, namely, Doiwala Sugar Company Limited
challenging the order dated 27.03.2015 passed by the
Uttarakhand Other Backward Class Commission directing non-1

appellant no.1 to grant compassionate appointment to the
appellant. The Single Judge has held that the Commission had
no power or authority to issue any such direction and that the
death of the father of the appellant took place in 1979,
therefore, the direction issued by the Commission for
compassionate appointment in 2015, after three decades, was
wholly unwarranted. As per own case of the petitioner, the
application for compassionate appointment was filed in the year
1985.
3. Irrespective of the grounds on which the writ petition
was allowed and the prayer for compassionate appointment was
declined, we observe that again there is inordinate delay and
laches in filing the instant appeal, and for which there is virtually
no explanation. Moreover, as per the affidavit of the appellant,
he is now aged 62 years and for this reason also, the claim for
compassionate appointment cannot be considered.
4. In view of the above, the delay condonation
application (IA No.1/2026) as well as the appeal stand
dismissed.
 (MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA, C. J.)
